body: Metals companies are price-takers. Profit equals spread (steel price minus iron ore and coking coal; aluminium LME minus alumina and power) times volume, so returns are set by global supply (above all China) and cost-curve position. Miners (Coal India, NMDC, Hindustan Zinc) earn price minus mining cost and are high-dividend, cash-generative and policy-exposed. Key metrics: EBITDA/tonne, volume and capacity growth, spread over raw material, cost-curve position (captive ore and coal), net debt/EBITDA, capex intensity, free cash flow, and for Tata Steel, Europe losses. Cycle drivers: China production and exports (2015 and 2023–25 export floods), global PMI, Indian infrastructure demand, trade defence (12% safeguard duty on flat steel from 2025), coking coal prices, LME aluminium and energy costs, and the USD. Lead indicators: China steel exports and property starts (NBS), SGX iron ore and coking coal futures, JPC (Joint Plant Committee) Indian steel consumption, the LME, Indian HRC prices (SteelMint/BigMint), DGTR trade remedy notices, the global manufacturing PMI. Winners (JSW on low-cost growth, Hindalco via Novelis downstream, Hindustan Zinc on cost leadership) had captive raw materials, the lowest cost quartile, and countercyclical balance sheets. Losers bought abroad at peak (Tata Corus 2007) or leveraged up into the downcycle (Essar, Bhushan, Monnet in 2015–17 IBC). Valuation: EV/EBITDA 4–8x on mid-cycle and P/B 0.7–2.5x. Buy when P/E is high or negative at the trough; sell when P/E is low at peak margins. Nov 2026: Q2 FY27 was strong (Tata Steel India PAT ₹5,055 cr, crude steel 6.21 mt +10%; JSW PAT ₹5,359 cr, EBITDA margin ~18.6%), and CLSA sees H2 FY27 momentum. Traps: low P/E at peak spreads.

data.business_model: Commodity spread x volume; cost-curve position decides through-cycle returns; miners earn price minus cost with royalty/policy risk.
data.current_state_nov_2026: Q2 FY27: Tata Steel India PAT ₹5,055 cr, India crude steel 6.21 mt (+10%); JSW Steel consolidated PAT ₹5,359 cr, record 7.27 mt crude steel, EBITDA margin ~18.6% vs 15.8%. 12% safeguard duty in place since 2025 (status should be rechecked); CLSA expects stronger H2 FY27.
data.cycle_drivers: China supply/exports, global PMI, domestic infra capex, trade remedies, input coal/ore prices, energy, USD.
key_metrics: Captive raw material share / cost-curve quartile
lead_indicators: SGX iron ore / coking coal futures
traps: Trade-protection-driven pricing that can be withdrawn
Capacity announcements funded by debt late in cycle
Miner dividend yield cut by royalty/policy changes
data.valuation: EV/EBITDA 4–8x mid-cycle; P/B 0.7x (2015–16, Mar 2020 troughs) to 2–2.5x (2008, 2021 peaks). Low P/E at peak spreads (2021–22) is the classic sell signal.
data.valuation_note: Historical valuation ranges and peak/trough dates come from general market history and were not re-verified against index factsheets this session. Treat them as unverified. Only the current-state figures are tied to the dated sources listed.
data.value_chain: Mining (ore, coal, bauxite) -> primary metal (blast furnace/EAF, smelter) -> downstream (coated, rolled, Novelis-type) -> end markets (construction ~60% for steel, auto, capital goods, packaging). Captive mines and downstream value-added products earn the most; non-integrated converters the least.
data.winners_vs_losers: Winners: lowest-cost quartile, captive raw materials, countercyclical capex, deleveraging in upcycles. Losers: overseas acquisitions at peak (2007), leverage into oversupply (2011–16), non-integrated converters.

title: Sector playbook: metals and mining
